resolution.reason: Wikidata’s 646 is the completion date of the Records (the QID’s item), not the journey. Xuanzang left Chang’an in 629, reached the north-western Indian lands c. 630, began his return in 643 and was back in 645 (Britannica).

resolution.reason: Wikidata gives a rounded generic point (13°N 77°E). Srirangapatna, Mysore’s capital under Hyder Ali and Tipu and the site of the decisive 1792 and 1799 sieges, is a more meaningful anchor 72 km away.

resolution.reason: Wikidata’s 31°N 74°E is a rounded Punjab point. The record is plotted at Gujrat, where the decisive battle of 21 February 1849 ended the war; Britannica confirms the Chillianwala–Gujrat sequence.

Both points are conventional: Wikidata’s Partition item sits at Calcutta. Independence was proclaimed in Delhi on 15 August 1947 (Nehru’s address, flag at the Red Fort), so Delhi is an equally or better-justified anchor.

The temple has no dedicatory inscription; two epigraphs credit 'Krishnaraja', i.e. Krishna I (r. c. 756–773), with most of it. The record spans his reign (756–773); Wikidata's 773 is only the end of that reign. Medium confidence with a note.

Wikidata's point is the centroid of Bangladesh (via its location property). The storm surge struck the coast and islands; Bhola Island, which gave the storm its name, was devastated across its southern half. Marker at Bhola Island.

Kanishka’s birth year is unrecorded; 100 is a labelled placeholder (confidence low, note). Wikidata’s 78 comes from the obsolete equation of his era with the Shaka era; Falk (2001) and Iranica place year 1 in 127/128 CE.
checked: Harry Falk, Silk Road Art and Archaeology 7 (2001)
Encyclopaedia Iranica: Kushan dynasty i. Dynastic history
